title: Ponavljanje
reviewerNotes: This full draft is ready for human review before publication.
storyBeat: Ana plans a solo weekend and drills frames from Lessons 15 through 20 at Amira's café.

vocabulary: Recycle idemo, karta, hoću, telefon, vikend, and plan for weekend talk.
Reuse često, autobus, račun, and još jednom in café and travel frames.
grammar: Practice Treba mi and Hoću for naming what you need and want.
Switch among Koliko košta?, Gdje je?, and Kakvo je vrijeme?
culture: Plan a solo weekend with postcards from Una, Bihać, or Jajce.
Treat this review as practice, not a new grammar system.

grammar.title: Remember Treba mi and Hoću
grammar.explanation: Treba mi names a need right now. Hoću names a wish. Keep both in the present tense, and add one familiar object after each verb.

grammar.title: Remember price, place, and weather questions
grammar.explanation: Koliko košta? Asks about price. Gdje je? Asks about place. Kakvo je vrijeme? Asks about weather. Choose the question that matches your weekend plan.

examples.english: How much does the ticket cost?

culture.title: Weekend planning with northwest postcards
culture.body: Ana spreads a weekend map beside her coffee and a postcard from Una or Bihać. The river towns of northwest Bosnia and Herzegovina offer waterfalls, old bridges, and quiet walks that suit a solo traveler well. Jajce appears on another card, with its fortress above the Pliva waterfall. Ana checks the weather, counts her budget, and writes a short plan on a napkin. Even a weekend alone still needs polite questions at a café and a ticket counter. These postcard places turn review lines into a real trip idea beyond Sarajevo.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson A. Practice need and wish frames
lessonBlocks.body: This review revisits frames from Lessons 15 through 20. Start with Treba mi and Hoću. Say Treba mi karta and Hoću vikend samo as full lines. Add telefon, plan, and vikend to your weekend story. Practice Koliko košta? Before you buy a bus ticket. Ana sits at Amira's café with a map and a Una postcard, naming what she needs and what she wants without any new grammar to learn. Repeat each frame još jednom until the need and the wish sound automatic.
tips: Keep Treba mi and Hoću with the object in one breath.
Say each frame još jednom before you switch to a question.
Stay in present tense for every weekend line.

lessonBlocks.title: Lesson B. Switch travel questions at the café
lessonBlocks.body: Now switch among three question frames. Ask Gdje je autobus? At the station. Ask Kakvo je vrijeme? Before a mountain walk. Finish café talk with Račun, molim when you pay. Emir and Amira help Ana test her solo plan while Mrvica watches the sugar bowl. Mix idemo with a place name and često with a habit from earlier lessons. You'll know the review is working when you can switch frames without translating in your head first. Stay in the present tense for every answer.
tips: Hear the question word before you choose your answer.
Add molim or hvala in every shop and café exchange.
Mix two old topics when one frame feels too easy.

funFacts.title: Una and Bihać suit a quiet weekend
funFacts.body: The Una River region in northwest Bosnia and Herzegovina offers green water and old towns like Bihać. A solo traveler can plan walks and river views without a big city crowd. Ana's postcard keeps the place in view while she reviews her travel lines.

funFacts.title: Jajce adds a waterfall stop
funFacts.body: Jajce sits above the Pliva waterfall and often shows up on traveler postcards. The fortress and old town give Ana a second weekend option beyond the Una valley. Real place names turn review vocabulary into real destinations.

funFacts.title: Treba mi stays a survival phrase
funFacts.body: Treba mi plus a noun is one of the fastest ways to name a need at a counter. You don't need a full conjugation table to buy a bus ticket. Pair it with molim and you'll sound ready for travel talk.

funFacts.title: Solo weekends still need polite lines
funFacts.body: Traveling alone doesn't mean traveling without manners. Račun, molim and hvala keep café and ticket talk friendly. Book 1 stays practical by mixing need, wish, and polite questions into one review session.

civicContext.title: Private rural bus lines collapse when routes stop paying
civicContext.body: Rural public transport in Bosnia and Herzegovina still depends heavily on private operators rather than a stable statewide network. When a mountain or village route stops turning a profit, companies cancel the line instead of absorbing the loss. Smaller places often lose daily service with no public replacement on the same timetable. The result is a patchwork map where a company's bottom line decides who can still reach work, school, or a clinic by bus.
